# AutoTrim

> AutoTrim is a desktop app for macOS and Windows that removes the silences and the hesitations ("um", "uh") from video and audio footage, entirely on the user's machine, and hands back one assembled timeline for Final Cut Pro, Adobe Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve, where every cut stays adjustable.

Key facts (updated October 2026, AutoTrim 2):

- Platforms: macOS and Windows (no Linux build). Most buyers edit in Final Cut Pro on a Mac.
- Final Cut Pro has no native silence removal. A few third-party effects can detect silence inside Final Cut Pro; AutoTrim works before the edit instead: it processes the whole shoot at once, removes hesitations as well as silences, and exports one FCPXML timeline.
- Workflow: drop all the footage of a shoot at once, AutoTrim processes the files in parallel and returns one merged timeline (not one file per clip to reassemble). Every cut can be adjusted in the editor, for example by dragging a clip edge to bring a breath back.
- Hesitations are detected in about ten languages, including English and French. A preview lets you listen to what was removed before exporting.
- Multicam and separate audio: AutoTrim finds the files of one take (several cameras, a separate audio recorder), syncs them, and only cuts when nobody is speaking. Audio-only files work too.
- Other exports: the already-cut video (one MP4 per source) or one numbered clip per cut (for CapCut).
- Privacy: all processing is local. Nothing is uploaded, unlike cloud tools such as Descript.
- Measured: across about 2,500 hours of footage run through AutoTrim, the median share of silence is one third.
- Pricing: free to try with unlimited previews; exporting requires a license: $15/month, $119/year, or $149 lifetime (one-time payment). 14-day money-back guarantee. Each license works on 2 computers.
- Made by Benjamin Code, a YouTuber and developer (https://www.youtube.com/@BenjaminCode).
